text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a common prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure and protect kidney function, but it can cause both mild and serious side effects.
These symptoms are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up too quickly)
Upper respiratory infections or cold-like symptoms (stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat)
Digestive issues (mild nausea, diarrhea, or indigestion)

text_blocks.snippet: Some reactions are uncommon but require prompt or emergency medical attention:

list.snippet: High potassium levels (hyperkalemia): Can cause muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or nausea (though it often has no symptoms).
Kidney problems: Signs include a dramatic decrease in urination, swelling in the hands, ankles, or feet, or severe fatigue.
Severe low blood pressure (hypotension): Can lead to fainting, confusion, or blurred vision.
Allergic reaction (angioedema): Dangerous swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, which makes it hard to breathe or swallow.
Severe birth defects: Losartan must not be taken during pregnancy.

text_blocks.snippet: For official prescribing guidance and safety details, you can review the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide.
